memory_update.text: PAR is the highest-priority underfollowed public candidate for restaurant first-party ordering, loyalty, POS, and customer-data infrastructure because its disclosed products map directly to the node.
NCR Voyix is a lower-attention restaurant POS and commerce infrastructure candidate, but the thesis depends on post-divestiture restaurant segment execution and recurring software growth.

Olo would have been the cleanest public pure-play for restaurant ordering, payments, and guest engagement, but it is no longer US-listed after Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition and delisting in September 2025.

For this node, the bottleneck is less physical supply and more control of customer access: POS, loyalty, order-routing, delivery integration, and payments vendors can become embedded infrastructure if restaurants prioritize first-party data and lower marketplace commission leakage.

node: Delivery marketplace access, first-party ordering, loyalty, POS, and restaurant customer-data infrastructure
summary: Expanded the underfollowed stock universe for restaurant customer-access infrastructure. The cleanest US-listed public exposures are not delivery marketplaces themselves but restaurant-specific POS, loyalty, ordering, payments, and drive-thru automation vendors. Olo would have been a high-quality pure-play reference for online ordering and guest data, but it was acquired by Thoma Bravo and delisted in September 2025, reducing the public pure-play universe. Current candidates skew toward PAR Technology, NCR Voyix, Toast, Shift4, and SoundHound-style restaurant automation/payment rails. This pass prioritizes underfollowed or less obvious public assets and treats broad fintech exposure cautiously unless restaurant-specific evidence is visible.
